blocks.h2: Signs Your Sump Pump Needs Attention
blocks.intro: A sump pump usually fails when you need it most. These are the warning signs worth acting on before the next storm:

tiles.h3: It Runs Constantly or Cycles On and Off
tiles.body: A pump that never stops, or kicks on and off every few seconds, is wearing itself out. The float switch, check valve or pump size is often the cause.
Grinding, rattling or humming without pumping points to a worn motor, a jammed impeller or debris in the pit.

tiles.h3: Water in the Pit but No Pumping
tiles.body: If the pit is filling and the pump isn't moving water, it's failed or the float is stuck. Call before the pit overflows.
Most sump pumps last around 7 to 10 years, less if they run often. An older pump in a finished basement is worth replacing on your schedule, not the storm's.

blocks.h2: Sump Pumps in Highland Park Homes
blocks.intro: The City of Highland Park's flood tips recommend inspecting sump pumps and battery backups before storm season. Here's why that advice matters in homes here.

items.body: The heaviest storms are also the ones most likely to knock out power. A sump pump with a battery backup keeps running when the power goes out, which is exactly when a primary pump without one stops.

Highland Park runs separate storm and sanitary sewers. A sump pump handles groundwater coming up under the slab or through the foundation. If water is coming up through a floor drain, that's the sewer side, and a different fix like an [overhead sewer system](/highland-park/overhead-sewer-systems).

Nearly half of Highland Park homes were built before 1960. Many have sump pits and discharge lines that were added or upgraded piecemeal over the years. We check the whole system: pit, pump, float, check valve and where the water goes.

blocks.h2: What We Do on a Sump Pump Call
blocks.intro: The process is the same for a pump that failed mid-storm or one you want replaced before the season starts.

steps.body: We check the pump, float switch, check valve and discharge line, not just the motor.
If a part fixes it, we'll tell you. If the pump is at the end of its life, we'll explain why and your options, including a battery backup.

steps.body: You get a flat-rate price before any work begins, with no surprise add-ons.

blocks.h2: Sump Pump Questions From Highland Park Homeowners

items.q: Do I need a battery backup sump pump?
items.preview: If your basement is finished, yes. Storms that fill the pit also knock out power.
items.answer: If you have a finished basement or store anything valuable down there, a battery backup is worth it. The storms that fill your sump pit fastest are also the ones most likely to cut power. The City of Highland Park's flood tips specifically recommend checking sump pumps and battery backups.

items.q: How often should a sump pump be replaced?
items.preview: Most last around 7 to 10 years. Older or noisy pumps are worth checking before storm season.
items.answer: Most sump pumps last around 7 to 10 years, less if they run often. If yours is more than 10 years old, runs constantly or makes new noises, it's worth having it checked before storm season.

items.q: Will a sump pump stop sewer backups?
items.preview: No. A sump pump handles groundwater. Sewer backups need a different fix.
items.answer: No. A sump pump removes groundwater. Water or sewage coming up through a floor drain is a sewer-side problem and needs a different fix, like clearing the line, a backflow valve or an [overhead sewer system](/highland-park/overhead-sewer-systems). We'll help you figure out which one you're dealing with.

items.q: How much does sump pump replacement cost?
items.preview: It depends on the pump, backup and pit condition. You get a flat price before we start.
items.answer: It depends on the pump type, whether you add a battery backup, the condition of the pit and discharge line, and access. We give you a flat-rate price before any work begins.
